decisions.question: Item 2 (S127): the contract does not say which error wins when a closed builder or handle also gets a bad argument (a foreign handle, a negative duration, an empty list, a dedup on an event read, a second sink). Which does the text state?

options.label: StateError first, as the code does
options.consequence: The handle paragraph and G15 say a builder or handle whose declaration has ended throws StateError whatever its arguments; every builder and handle method of the shipped package calls _checkOpen() before any argument check, so no code changes; one new G15 case pins it

options.label: ArgumentError first
options.consequence: a code change in nidana.model (every method's check order) plus a G15 amendment, outside the sweep's rule

options.label: leave it open
options.consequence: a second reading of the paragraph stays possible, and a reordering defect passes every case (D9 and D10 in the dry run)

decisions.chosen: StateError first, as the code does
decisions.why: The facts probe shows StateError in all eight combinations (C1 to C8), and the code's choice is sound: a closed builder records nothing whatever it is given, and the StateError names the actual misuse, a handle or builder kept past its declaration. Both errors are programming errors and recording has one implementation by design, so no consumer depends on the other order.
evidence: packages/nidana_dart_contracts/lib/src/topology/builder.dart and handle.dart (_checkOpen first in every method)
docs/auto-run/experiments/sweep-topology-dsl/output.txt F C1 to C9, D9, D10

options.label: ArgumentError without calling the combiner, in prose under The plan and in G11
options.consequence: states what both apply bodies do (a length check that throws ArgumentError.value before the combiner); the Interface's doc comments stay identical to the package's, which copied them

options.label: the same rule in the apply doc comment (S127's proposed wording)

options.label: also state TypeError for a value of another type
options.consequence: true of the shipped package (facts A1 to A3) and pinned by its own test, but not routed here and a second rule to pin

decisions.chosen: ArgumentError without calling the combiner, in prose under The plan and in G11
decisions.why: The facts show ArgumentError (not a RangeError) for a short and a long list in all three forms and no combiner call (A1 to A4). The case uses a list longer than the inputs as well, because RangeError is an ArgumentError and a missing check would otherwise pass with a short list alone (A5; D11 and D12 fail only through the long and empty lists). TypeError is left unstated: the item asks about length only.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/sweep-topology-dsl/output.txt F A1 to A6, D11, D12

decisions.question: Item 1, stages left behind after a rejected call: G11 says each call adds exactly one stage and says nothing of a call that throws; a call that records its stage, or marks its handle consumed, or counts its state topic as written, before a check that fails passes every committed case. Is there a stated rule to pin, and if not what does the text state?

options.label: state the code's choice: a call that throws records nothing
options.consequence: The handle paragraph, Recording and G14 say a call that throws adds no stage and no sink and a declaration that catches its error plans as if the call had not been made; the shipped package runs every check before _addStage or _addSink; one G14 case pins it against four seeded defects

options.label: leave it open
options.consequence: an implementation could leave a stage behind, which then fails planOf with StateError only when the declaration catches the error, or a stage that reaches no sink could pass because a rejected sink marked it consumed

decisions.chosen: state the code's choice: a call that throws records nothing
decisions.why: Atomic calls are the only reading under which a caught error leaves the plan meaningful, and the code already does it (facts R1 to R3). An uncaught error propagates from planOf either way, so only a declaration that catches can tell the difference, which is why no consumer can depend on the other behavior. A careful engineer would not have asked.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/sweep-topology-dsl/output.txt F R1 to R3, D3, D8, D13, D14

decisions.question: Item 1, an identity-based one-sink check: G14 says a second sink on 'one StateTopic' throws, without saying how two topics are one. The new case could also pin that a StateTopic<num> of the same name is another topic. How far does the touch go?

options.label: equal under topic-model@v1 G7, pin only the topic built apart
options.consequence: G14 and The builder name G7 equality; the case builds a StateTopic<int> of the same name with another initial value at run time and expects ArgumentError for write then write and reduceInto then write; it says nothing about two topics of one name and different value types

options.label: also pin that another value type is another topic
options.consequence: matches the package test, but fixes in the conformance suite an answer to the open S132 item (two topics of one name whose value types render alike break topology-ir@v1's well-formedness), which a recording rule for name collisions would reverse

decisions.chosen: equal under topic-model@v1 G7, pin only the topic built apart
decisions.why: Topics have value equality (G7), so identity is not a sound reading, and the code uses a Set under topic == (facts S1, S2; D4 fails the new case). The other-value-type half would preempt the S132 item, which belongs to topology-ir@v1's touch or to the owner; the Versioning entry names it as left as it was.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md Routed to later phases, the entry from S132's final review

decisions.question: S127's further seeded defects: a builder closed only when declare returns normally (the text says 'has returned'), and a foreign handle told apart by its builder being closed rather than by identity (a handle of a declaration still running, passed into a nested planOf). State and pin them?

options.label: state both as the code does and pin them
options.consequence: The handle, G14 and G15 say a builder closes when its declaration ends by returning or by throwing, and that a handle is another builder's whether its declaration is still running or has ended; one G15 and one G14 case

options.label: leave them to the package tests
options.consequence: a second implementation or a regression closes the builder only on a normal return, or accepts a running declaration's handle in a nested planOf, and passes the contract

decisions.chosen: state both as the code does and pin them
decisions.why: planOf closes the builder in a finally block and _checkMade compares builders by identity (facts T1 to T3, N1). 'has returned' was the only word that let the throwing case read otherwise; 'another builder' already meant identity. Both fail their seeded defect only with the new cases (D5, D6).

decisions.question: S127's list defects: a merge that keeps the caller's list, and combineAll handing its combiner a modifiable cast view. The Interface says the input lists and combineAll's list are unmodifiable; does the text also say the stage's lists are copies taken at the call?

options.label: unmodifiable copies taken at the call
options.consequence: The plan and G11 say so; one G11 case clears the caller's list after the call, adds to every list the stage holds and to the list combineAll's combiner gets, and expects UnsupportedError

options.label: unmodifiable only
options.consequence: a read-only view of the caller's list would pass, and a declaration that changed its list after the call would change the stage's inputs, bypassing G14's foreign-handle check and the reaches-a-sink check

decisions.chosen: unmodifiable copies taken at the call
decisions.why: G11 already says a stage holds the handles it was given; a live view lets it hold handles it was never given. The code takes List.unmodifiable copies in _checkMade and a fresh List<T>.unmodifiable for combineAll's combiner (facts L1 to L5; D2 and D7 fail only the new case).
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/sweep-topology-dsl/output.txt F L1 to L5, D2, D7

experiments.finding: Facts: StateError wins over every argument error on a closed builder or handle (C1 to C8); apply throws a plain ArgumentError for a short and a long list in all three forms and calls no combiner, TypeError for a value of another type (A1 to A6); caught calls leave a plan of one stage and one sink, and a stage passed only to a rejected second sink still fails planOf with StateError (R1 to R3); a StateTopic built apart is equal, not identical, and its second sink throws ArgumentError (S1, S2); a nested planOf given a running declaration's handle throws ArgumentError (N1); after a declaration throws, its builder and handle throw StateError (T1 to T3); stage lists are unmodifiable copies and combineAll's combiner gets an unmodifiable list (L1 to L5); visitors bind each class's type arguments (V1, V2). Fixtures: committed 24/24; with S152's cases 31/31 (28 fixtures) against the shipped package; fifteen seeded defects (D1 to D15) each pass the committed cases restricted to their guarantee and fail exactly one new case; the restored copy equals HEAD and passes 31/31. P: fresh, dart run and the script form both start (exit 64 from the program); stale (a member pubspec.yaml newer than pubspec.lock), dart run exits 255 before the program starts and the script form starts; dart pub get --enforce-lockfile --offline changes no mtime and dart run still exits 255.
